races.name: Tattersalls £40,000 Ebf Maiden Fillies' Stakes (gbb Race)
Zyn Frontrunner Finish Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Crown Of Oaks
runners_data.note: William Haggas's 4-y-o returns on 62-day break having won at this exact trip on Good ground (1/8f/GOO), and her OR-104 mark combined with Callum Rodriguez's positive front-of-midfield approach makes her the leading prominent contender; Haggas T14 of 8/47 underpins confidence.
runners_data.comment: Crown Of Oaks won three times in his last five starts, including a victory two runs back, and has experience of today's distance and going — the chief concern is whether 62 days off the track has left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: King's Charter
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's 4-y-o has won twice at 10f on Good ground and is the sole confirmed leader here, meaning he gets a soft, uncontested lead; the 169-day layoff is a concern, Toby Moore (7lb claim) adds risk, and his STYLE_FIT tag reflects that his odds may be inflated by positional gift rather than ability.
runners_data.comment: King's Charter has distance and going experience in his favour, and a second two starts back gives him a profile worth considering, though a lengthy 169-day absence is the obvious concern and he carries 142 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Involvement
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's 5-y-o has solid course-and-distance form (3/12f/GOO) and is 28 days fresh; Mason Paetel (3lb claim) partners a horse who races prominently, which is a viable spot in this field, though the recent form string of 134638 shows he finds one or two too strong.

runners_data.name: Cash
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer is the key angle — the master of patient, late-delivery tactics on a 7-y-old who carries OR-99; running from the hold-up position in what could be a moderate-paced race is a tactical risk, but Spencer's course awareness and the Good ground suit a sustained late rattle.
runners_data.comment: Has run over today's trip and going before, which makes Cash a leading player here, and our rating has him top of this 13-runner field; yet to score in his last five starts and 77 days off the track are the concerns to weigh.

runners_data.name: Kokbastau
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's lightly-raced 3-y-o has won his last two (1/12f/STA, 1/12f/STA) and steps onto Good turf having previously only placed once on this surface; the step up from stalls tracks to Sandown's unique configuration is the unknown, but a prominent racing style positions him ideally if he transfers that form.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Kokbastau is hard to fancy despite carrying a 102 official rating, and his speed rating of 77 gives little encouragement; in his favour, he arrives in form with back-to-back wins in his last four starts and has run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Tribal Chief
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's 5-y-o is a hold-up type whose best efforts came at shorter trips (3/7f/GOO, 3/8f/GOO) and recent form over today's 10f-12f range has been modest; OR-92 and a trainer with 0/6 in the 14-day window offer little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Tribal Chief has run over today's trip and going, and back-to-back thirds three and four starts back show he can find the frame, but he's winless in his last five and an unplaced effort last time out is a concern; 130 lb from stall two makes this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Flying Frontier
runners_data.note: James Tate's 6-y-o is a natural prominent racer whose trips at 10f-12f on Good ground are consistent (four placings across those conditions), but with so many prominent types in this field he is unlikely to secure that forward position; at OR-91 and with a STYLE_FIT discount, his chance hinges on outrunning his mapped role.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Flying Frontier has at least shown some consistency at fourth on two occasions in that spell, and he has experience of today's distance and going; carrying 129 lb from stall 12 while ranked ninth of thirteen, he faces a stiff task to improve markedly here.

runners_data.name: Alcarath
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's booking for Alan King's 4-y-o is the standout jockey upgrade, and his form shows five consecutive top-5 finishes at 9f-10f on Good ground; naturally prominent, he will be squeezed for early position in this congested field but Murphy's ability to find a pitch makes him the most dangerous of the redistributed runners.
runners_data.comment: Shaped well enough when runner-up last time out, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but 78 days off the track and a middle-ranking profile among 13 rivals means he needs to find a gear he hasn't shown in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: Love Beach
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's 4-y-o won at 10f on Good ground (1/10f/GOO) and has placed three times on soft, showing she handles cut, but Good here is fine; her true front-end preferences are compromised by the crowded prominent group, and Kaiya Fraser's inexperience is an additional layer of concern.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well out of the reckoning on our figures and unplaced last time out after 78 days off, Love Beach is hard to fancy despite carrying a workable weight from stall five; he has run over today's distance and going before, and a win in his last five starts shows he can find the frame.

runners_data.name: My Love Is King
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's 3-y-o carries a visor for the first time and has two successive runner-up finishes at 10f on Good ground; Robert Havlin's route will be to sit just off the pace prominently, and the headgear switch suggests connections want more focus from a horse whose form trend is in the right direction.
runners_data.comment: Ran to a high level two and three starts back with back-to-back seconds, and he has a win four starts back, but an eighth last time out after 72 days off is a concern; has run over today's trip and going, and the trainer is striking at 26% lately.

runners_data.name: The Glen Rovers
runners_data.note: William Buick is a significant booking for Lucy Wadham's yard (T14: 1/2), and this 7-y-o posted a recent 4th at 12f on Good (4/12f/GOO) on this same trip profile; purely a hold-up type with a mixed sim-going record (2/15), he needs a strong pace to set up his late run, which looks unlikely here.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 13 on our figures and with back-to-back ninths in his last two starts before a fourth most recently, The Glen Rovers has plenty to prove here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a win four starts back shows he can find the line first.

runners_data.name: Stem
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's 4-y-o has a broadly prominent style squeezed back into midfield by the weight of traffic ahead; a 10f Good win is on his card (1/10f/GOO) but his last four runs show 0, 10, 4, 13 — inconsistent, and at OR-89 with a STYLE_FIT note, he needs things to go wrong for others.
runners_data.comment: Stem won two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, with 21 days since that unplaced return keeping him fresh; the concern is a trainer operating at just 5% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Gonna Fly
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's 3-y-o has two wins on record (1/10f/GOO, 1/8f/SOF) and Rossa Ryan can be positive, but he is a natural prominent type operating out of his preferred position in this crowded field; the youth and upside at just 3 is appealing, but at OR-93 and with his style compromised, he is more of an each-way shape than a pace-map winner.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, Gonna Fly faces a stiff ask, and back-to-back finishes of fifth and ninth in his last two starts make him hard to fancy at present, though he has winning form in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: King's Charter is the lone confirmed front-runner and, crucially, faces no genuine rival for the lead — with one sustainable gallop set from the front on Good turf over 1m2f at Sandown, this shapes as a controlled, unhurried affair that will not be run at a punishing tempo. Crown Of Oaks, Kokbastau, Involvement and My Love Is King are the genuine prominent types who will likely settle just off King's Charter's shoulder, giving the race a compact, mid-pace dynamic where position off the bend into the straight becomes critical. The field contains significantly more prominent-type runners than the race can accommodate — Flying Frontier, Alcarath, Love Beach, Stem and Gonna Fly all carry natural prominent tendencies but are mapped to midfield because King's Charter and the rated OR leaders will occupy the front ranks; of those bumped back, Alcarath (Oisin Murphy booking) and Gonna Fly (Beckett, 3-y-o) are best-placed to recover ground if gaps appear. A sustainable, uncontested lead with a mid-race tempo strongly favours horses who can sit second or third, travel comfortably, and produce a sustained finish from the two-furlong pole — the prominent-to-handy profile is the one to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If King's Charter dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the race lacks a genuine pace injection until the home straight.
scenarios.body: King's Charter sets an untroubled rhythm, and the horses sitting on his girth travelling smoothly into the Sandown straight benefit from not burning petrol chasing anything; those with the best ORs and strongest form at the trip pounce from 2f out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If King's Charter's controlled fractions are so slow that no chaser has the acceleration to reel him in.
scenarios.body: An undercooked early pace leaves pursuers having to find a meaningful change of gear at 2f out that the Good ground alone cannot generate quickly enough; King's Charter, given a soft lead and a Toby Moore positive ride, simply gallops rivals into submission.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If a genuine pace injection mid-race stretches the field and the leaders are left vulnerable to horses charging from further back.
scenarios.body: A competitive pocket forms in the leading group around the 5f mark, burning out front-runners and leaving the race wide open for horses who have been conserving energy in midfield; Cash (Jamie Spencer, patient tactics) and The Glen Rovers (William Buick) have profiles that benefit from an unexpectedly fast early sectional.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Prominent Jam
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded prominent group produces a traffic-affected, uneven race where the field concertinas and position is lost mid-race.
scenarios.body: Multiple horses hunting for the same prominent berth force an uneven tempo that scrambles expected order; redistributed types like Gonna Fly or Alcarath, who find daylight late, could profit if Murphy or Ryan produce well-timed deliveries.

watchPoints.text: King's Charter (169-day absence) — if he shows any rustiness in the first furlong and surrenders the lead cheaply, the entire pace map collapses and no single horse inherits a clean, uncontested front, triggering chaos in the prominent group.

Oisin Murphy on Alcarath — Murphy will aggressively seek a prominent position despite redistribution; watch for him pushing forward out of the gates and forcing rival jockeys to react, which could lift the early fractions beyond King's Charter's comfort zone.

My Love Is King (visor first-time) — headgear switches on John & Thady Gosden horses in handicaps often signal a meaningful move; if the visor produces sharper early pace from this horse, it increases pressure on King's Charter from the second position.

Cash and The Glen Rovers are the only true hold-up horses with genuine late-run credentials; if the pace dynamic is even moderate, track how much ground they are losing through the first half-mile — if it is excessive (more than 8 lengths), their scenarios close down entirely.

The cluster of OR-89 to OR-93 redistributed runners (Gonna Fly, Alcarath, Love Beach, Flying Frontier, Stem) will all be bidding for the same early ground — a crowded, bumping first furlong is plausible and worth monitoring for any horse that loses its action or position critically before the race settles.

races.name: Betmgm Atalanta Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Kon Tiki
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a strong mile record at pattern level on good ground — two wins from five similar-going starts and a 35-day freshener suits; Oisin Murphy gives him a sharp tactical brain in a congested early contest.|
runners_data.comment: Kon Tiki arrives on the back of a win last time out, has experience of today's trip and going, and her rating of 115 marks her as a lively danger — the main concern is whether 135 lb from stall one will blunt her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Love Dynasty
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's mare won over this course-and-distance trip but faces a 84-day break and a field where her natural prominent pitch is already oversubscribed — she is likely to race further back than ideal, compromising her chance, and her sole good-ground form shows only a second.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts yet consistently competitive, Love Dynasty has run over today's trip and going and her rating of 113 suggests she holds strong claims from stall three; the concern is 84 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Maeva
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who is first run in 134 days for Charlie Fellowes — the layoff is a real concern, the headgear note adds intrigue, but she has won twice on softer surfaces and good ground figures are modest; Paddy Bradley must produce a patient, well-timed run from the rear.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and returning from a 134-day break, Maeva is hard to fancy despite two wins in her last five starts; she has run over today's trip and going before, but back-to-back sixth and fifth most recently make her difficult to support at this level.

runners_data.name: Noche Clasica
runners_data.note: One of the genuine deep closers in the field but her recent Sandown run produced only fifth, and a flat good-going surface is not where she has built her best form — Edward Bethell's yard is in good nick (7 from 29 over 14 days) and Robert Havlin knows her well, but she needs the pace to properly collapse.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten into fifth last time out and unplaced two starts back, Noche Clasica arrives on a tricky patch of form, though she has winning ability — a winner on two occasions in her last five starts — and has run over today's trip and going before, returning after 21 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Calendar Girl
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in five starts on good ground and has won over a mile already this season; Owen Burrows' three-year-old is the standout prominent type on form and Callum Rodriguez won on her last time — she has every right to be close to the pace and fire off it.|
runners_data.comment: Calendar Girl arrives in red-hot form, winning four of her last five starts, and having run over today's distance and going before, conditions pose no concern; drawn in stall five and carrying 126 lb, she looks primed on a 21-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Cap Santa Lucia
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's filly won her maiden at this distance on good ground and is a natural press-the-leader type — she cannot get that berth as freely in this field, so Spencer will likely nurse her into a tracking position and hope to challenge late rather than dictate.|
runners_data.comment: Rated well below her official mark on our figures and ranked ninth of ten, Cap Santa Lucia is hard to fancy at the weights, though she was a winner two starts back and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Moon Target
runners_data.note: Luke Morris partners a genuine hold-up performer for Sir Mark Prescott; form figures of 738-43 are modest but the yard has been active and winning (6 from 18 over 14 days) — she needs bunched late traffic and a truly run race, not a controlled So Regal procession.|
runners_data.comment: Moon Target arrives 27 days fresh, handles today's distance and going, and her third last time out hints at capability; rated 110, she shapes as a genuine threat from stall 2 carrying 126 lb, though being winless in her last five starts is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Pacific Mission
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's three-year-old has been consistent without winning — five placed efforts in similar company — and races in a hood; she wants a prominent role but so do four others, so Callum Hutchinson may find himself squeezed for room early in what has been a placed-heavy career so far.|
runners_data.comment: Pacific Mission has been consistent without landing the prize, finishing second three times and third once in her last five starts, yet to win in recent form; she has run over today's trip and going, carries 126 lb from stall 10, and a rating of 104 keeps her competitive at this level.

runners_data.name: Secret Of Life
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in three starts including two over a mile, Ralph Beckett's filly arrives fresh (56 days) and with plenty of upside — Rossa Ryan can place her close to the pace, and an OR of 102 likely understates her ceiling; the unknown is whether a first Group-level test reveals a ceiling.|
runners_data.comment: Three-timer chaser stepping out after 56 days off, and her speed rating of 84 leaves her looking exposed against stronger company on our figures despite that eye-catching hat-trick; has run over today's trip, which counts in her favour, but she's hard to fancy ranked eighth of ten.

runners_data.name: So Regal
runners_data.note: William Buick's mount is the sole front-runner and will set the tempo from flag to line on good ground — 106 days since last run is the only query, but two wins from four good-going starts and a Gosden polish suggest she arrives ready; controls everything if allowed to dictate unmolested.|
runners_data.comment: So Regal won two of her last four starts and finished second last time out, showing clear ability, but 106 days off the track is a fitness question and she heads into a competitive field ranked seventh of ten on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: So Regal is the sole confirmed leader and, ridden by William Buick for the powerful Gosden yard, is likely to stride out from the front and control a measured, unhurried gallop on good ground over this Sandown mile. The prominent group is congested — Calendar Girl, Kon Tiki, Pacific Mission and Secret Of Life all want to race close to the pace, creating a genuine scramble for position in the first two furlongs that could briefly sharpen the tempo before So Regal settles into her rhythm. Cap Santa Lucia and Love Dynasty are natural prominent types but cannot all occupy those berths simultaneously; Cap Santa Lucia with Jamie Spencer is best placed to exploit gaps from a tracking position, while Love Dynasty is most likely to be shuffled back against her will. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than this race shape can accommodate, meaning the riders for Cap Santa Lucia and Love Dynasty will face a tactical compromise — Spencer may steal a march, but Love Dynasty is likeliest to race genuinely out of role. With a single front-runner setting a controlled, honest pace and a congested midfield behind, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-handy types with a turn of foot, particularly those who can settle just off the leader and pounce from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If So Regal dictates an uncontested, even gallop and one of the prominent chasers lands a winning blow turning in.
scenarios.body: So Regal sets fractions she controls entirely, and the horse best positioned just off her shoulder — Calendar Girl, Kon Tiki or Secret Of Life — has enough in reserve to accelerate past her from the two-furlong pole on good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady and So Regal's rivals are caught flat-footed when she quickens approaching the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: With a light weight and Buick dictating every yard, So Regal could manufacture enough of a cushion that the prominent chasers simply cannot close the gap on good ground that doesn't fully aid hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Overhaul Field
scenarios.trigger: If the early prominence battle creates a messy, fast opening half-mile that burns off those racing keenly close to the pace.
scenarios.body: A scrambled early pace would compress the race into a two-furlong sprint and benefit the genuine hold-up horses who have been held off the bridle; Noche Clasica and Moon Target are the authentic deep closers here, though their recent form demands everything goes right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaos, Spoiler Result
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion behind So Regal causes interference and shuffling two to three furlongs out, allowing a midfield type to thread through.
scenarios.body: Cap Santa Lucia, forced out of her natural prominent role and ridden by the tactically astute Jamie Spencer, is the most likely beneficiary of positional chaos, picking off tiring rivals between horses.

watchPoints.text: Watch the opening two furlongs for a prominence battle between Calendar Girl, Kon Tiki, Pacific Mission and Secret Of Life — four horses wanting the same ground behind So Regal means significant traffic risk between the two and three-furlong markers.

So Regal's layoff of 106 days is the biggest unknown in the race shape — if she is not quite at her peak, Buick may let her coast rather than push, compressing the race into a late sprint that overturns the tactical picture entirely.

Cap Santa Lucia is unlikely to secure her natural forward position with Jamie Spencer aboard — watch for Spencer exploiting gaps on the inside rail from a tracking position, which he excels at when forced to improvise tactically.

Love Dynasty has not run for 84 days and is likely to race further back than her natural style demands — if she is short of peak fitness after the layoff, she could fade from the rear rather than deliver a meaningful late challenge.

Noche Clasica's trainer Edward Bethell has had seven winners from 29 runners over the last 14 days — monitor late market moves on Robert Havlin's mount, as Bethell's yard is operating in sharp form even if her individual form figures are patchy.|

races.name: Betmgm Solario Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Alfred Wallace
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's hold-up specialist has won twice over this course and distance on good ground, is 6-from-6 in similar going, and Kieran Shoemark is a strong booking; the moderate OR of 104 is the main query but the race shape sets up perfectly for his late run.
runners_data.comment: Alfred Wallace won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a strong contender from stall seven off 129 lb; a fourth last time out is the only minor blemish on a profile that warrants plenty of respect, with our rating of 110 marking him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Breacher
runners_data.note: A wide-margin winner on his only start over 7f on good ground 60 days ago, the layoff is the obvious concern for the Muir & Grassick yard but the form reads well; genuinely lightly raced and the sim-going record is a clean 1/1 — one to watch carefully.
runners_data.comment: Breacher won last time out but has been off the track for 60 days, which raises a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and carries 129 lb from stall four, though a rating of 89 leaves him with ground to make up on the principals.

runners_data.name: Dover Street
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's runner has been placed on both career starts but both came on softer surfaces, and this good ground and the competitive group stage are new tests; Pat Dobbs rides and he tends to sit handy, which could see him caught up in the prominent battle.
runners_data.comment: Dover Street has been winless in his last two starts, finishing fifth two runs back before a runner-up effort last time, and our figures rank him eighth of nine here, making him hard to fancy despite the distance experience and a quick eight-day turnaround keeping him fit.

runners_data.name: Firehorse
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner for S Woods who was beaten in his last two on good ground after winning over 6f on standard; will contest the lead aggressively with Sonic Angel and the question is whether that early duel leaves him with enough for the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Firehorse bolts in a win three starts back and returns in sharp order just 17 days later, carrying 129 lb from stall 5 with experience over today's trip backing his claims; the concern is that two subsequent efforts have seen him regress to fifth and sixth.

runners_data.name: Green Sovereign
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's hold-up filly has only one win in four starts on good ground (1/4 sim-going, 0W0P) but won over 6f on soft before stepping up in trip; Kaiya Fraser rides and a strong gallop would help her get competitive at a price.
runners_data.comment: Green Sovereign showed he can win at this level with a victory three starts back, and has experience over today's trip carrying 129 lb from stall two; the main risk is a return to the disappointing efforts last time out and two starts back.

runners_data.name: Kodiac City
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer on an unbeaten Jamie Spencer mount — the jockey's trademark of rating a horse and delivering late is well-suited to this contested pace, and the single win over 8f on standard leaves a trip question at 7f on turf.
runners_data.comment: Kodiac City won last time out and returns in good order on 23 days' rest, but he ranks seventh of nine on our figures and the weight of 129 lb makes life harder still.

runners_data.name: Mia Fantasia
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly has won twice over 7f and loves this trip, but with more prominent types than the race can accommodate she is unlikely to get her natural front-of-midfield berth; her best form (1W2P sim-going) has come when travelling freely, and being crowded back will test her finishing.
runners_data.comment: Mia Fantasia won last time out and has run over today's trip, returning on a snappy nine-day turnaround in cracking heart; the main concern is whether 129 lb from stall ten will blunt his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Rock Montreal
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's unbeaten colt won over this exact trip and going profile (1/7f/GOO) and William Buick's booking is the standout jockey engagement of the race; the OR of 120 is among the joint-highest and the horse is unexposed, making him a prime beneficiary if the prominent group can survive the early pace.
runners_data.comment: Rock Montreal won last time out but is ranked bottom of this nine-runner field on our figures, and his speed rating of 77 offers little encouragement despite the experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Sergei Diaghilev
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's runner is 2W in 3 starts on good ground and has already shown versatility in being prominent over different trips; a trainer running at 8 from 50 in the past fortnight is worth noting, but the quality of the operation means this lightly raced colt must be respected.

runners_data.name: Sonic Angel
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in two starts for Simon & Ed Crisford with Oisin Murphy up, both wins on standard ground — the step up to good turf at Sandown is untested but the combination of Murphy and a confirmed front-runner who has never been headed makes her the most likely to control the pace rather than just contest it.
runners_data.comment: Sonic Angel arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and a 10-day turnaround keeps him fresh, but 129 lb from stall one and a ranking of fifth of nine suggest his task is no formality despite the in-form profile.

races.paceDynamic: Firehorse and Sonic Angel are both confirmed front-runners and will fight for the early lead from the gates, creating a genuinely contested gallop over Sandown's 7f on good ground — this is not a race where either will settle for a passenger role. Four of the ten runners want prominent positions, meaning the first two furlongs will see significant pressure as Kodiac City, Dover Street, Rock Montreal and Sergei Diaghilev all push to track the leaders, creating congestion and potential interference between the 2f and 3f markers. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions — Mia Fantasia is the runner most likely to be shuffled back from her preferred prominent berth, with the front two slots almost certainly monopolised by Firehorse and Sonic Angel. With a truly-run gallop virtually guaranteed, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and genuine closers who can sit off the pace, conserve energy in the early exchanges, and produce a sustained finish — Alfred Wallace and Green Sovereign profile best for that pattern.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Firehorse and Sonic Angel cut out a genuine gallop and the prominent group burns energy fighting for position in the first three furlongs.
scenarios.body: The honest pace softens up the leaders and the prominent runners who jostled early, leaving the race wide open for hold-up horses to pick them off in the final two furlongs. Alfred Wallace and Breacher, both capable of landing a late blow, sit ideally placed to benefit from this most likely race shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the pace from the front is strong but not suicidal, allowing the prominent trio to travel well in behind and strike entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Rock Montreal, Kodiac City and Sergei Diaghilev all won their sole starts and carry the highest ORs in the field — if they find a rhythm in the prominent group they have the class to overwhelm rivals with ease. William Buick's hands-and-heels style on Rock Montreal could be particularly telling if the race is run at a competitive but controlled clip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sticks On
scenarios.trigger: If Sonic Angel or Firehorse can dictate at a deceptively even gallop that flatters their stamina and blunts the closers' finishing kick.
scenarios.body: Sonic Angel's unbeaten record and Oisin Murphy's ability to control fractions gives her the best chance of rating the race to suit, stealing a march entering the final furlong. At 7f on good ground with a field fighting for position behind, a horse ahead of trouble and relaxed on the front end is genuinely hard to reel in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail, Chaos Ensues
scenarios.trigger: If early scrimmaging in the prominent group causes interference, checks, or wide running that neutralises the hold-up horses too, leaving the race to a fortunate traveller.
scenarios.body: A race run at extreme pace with widespread traffic trouble could randomise the result and hand the race to whichever runner avoids the carnage and finds the clearest passage — Sergei Diaghilev's Aidan O'Brien angle and proven Sandown-trip form makes him a plausible beneficiary of a muddled scenario.

watchPoints.text: Firehorse and Sonic Angel will clash for the lead from the off — watch for a fierce early duel in the first furlong that could see both use excess energy and compromise their finishing ability.

Four runners (Kodiac City, Dover Street, Rock Montreal, Sergei Diaghilev) all want prominent positions — watch for severe congestion and potential for bumping or checking between the 5f and 4f markers as they jockey for rail positions.

Mia Fantasia is unlikely to secure her natural prominent pitch given the traffic ahead of her — watch whether Marco Ghiani elects to drop her in or push forward regardless, as either choice significantly changes her race.
Breacher has been off 60 days for a yard (Muir & Grassick) that is 2 from 12 in the past fortnight — watch the market move closely as a strong drift could signal the layoff is telling.

Alfred Wallace is 10 days since his last run and fits this race shape as well as any runner on the card — watch where Shoemark positions him early; if he sits last or second-last, the contested gallop plays directly into his hands.

races.name: Download The BetMGM App Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Defence Minister
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Hamad Al Jehani with Callum Rodriguez in the saddle; finished 1st on soft at Sandown over 7f and has placed form on good, though recent runs at this course show he needs things to set up perfectly from the rear — 31 days off is not a concern given he won fresh.
runners_data.comment: Defence Minister won four starts back and has run over today's trip, arriving here 31 days on from his last outing; rated 100 and ranked top of the field, he is the one to beat despite a patchy recent profile.

runners_data.name: Desert Shadow
runners_data.note: Won last two starts over 7f-8f on good ground for Saeed bin Suroor, and Oisin Murphy's booking is a significant upgrade; visor noted in headgear, has wide draw risk on a straight track, but his form figures of -05211 show a horse rapidly progressive and dangerous if the pace develops late.
runners_data.comment: Desert Shadow has winning form — back-to-back victories in his last two starts — but our figures rank him eighth of ten, and the burden of 139 lb makes it hard to fancy despite that decent recent momentum and experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Silver Ghost
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Emma Lavelle, placed in three of last five over 7f on good, but yet to win at the top level of this OR; Ray Dawson takes over and the concern here is that his pattern of finishing second and third without winning suggests he may lack the decisive gear to break through.
runners_data.comment: Silver Ghost arrives on the back of a placed effort three starts back and a podium finish four starts back, and with experience over today's trip and a rating of 96 she shapes as a genuine danger carrying 136 lb from stall 2; the risk is that she has been winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Shameful
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's runner returns from a 436-day absence — that layoff is the critical flag; has placed twice over 7f on good when fresh and has strong hold-up-to-prominent style, and Rossa Ryan navigates well in small fields, but the fitness question off that long break must temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Shameful showed real quality when winning and posting back-to-back runner-up finishes in his last four starts, and he has run over today's trip before; the concern is a 436-day absence, which leaves fitness the obvious question mark.

runners_data.name: God Of War
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's gelding is a genuine hold-up type by nature — his style_fit score reflects that he is unlikely to replicate his best from a midfield berth on a track where the pace is modest; headgear (p) and a 15-day turnaround suggest readiness, but his last six runs read 4-4-0-5-7 away from his best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, God Of War has at least run over today's trip and returns on a handy 15-day turnaround carrying 134 lb from stall six, though a seventh last time out makes it hard to fancy him strongly against this field.

runners_data.name: Storm Free
runners_data.note: James Tate's consistent performer with two wins on good ground over 7f and a placed effort recently; Lewis Edmunds rides and Storm Free slots naturally into a prominent role off which he can exploit a slow tempo — won on this surface and trip and his profile fits the dominant pace shape of this race.
runners_data.comment: Storm Free won last time out and also boasts a win in his last five starts, bringing strong recent form into this, and he has run over today's trip before; the main risk is whether his level holds after three below-par efforts sandwiched between those victories.

runners_data.name: Monarch's Gold
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's three-year-old carries 131lbs and has been placed at this trip on good; Sean Levey retains the ride and the horse's form of 202935 shows respectable consistency without finding the win button — youngest in the field and the weight is a leveller.
runners_data.comment: Monarch's Gold returns 27 days on from a third two starts back, though winless in his last six and that ninth three starts back tempers optimism; he has run over today's trip, carries 131 lb from stall one, and his rating of 94 suggests a shade of unexploited potential.

runners_data.name: Huscal
runners_data.note: Charles Hills's gelding is a hold-up specialist by style (headgear: t) who has placed four times at 7f-8f on good, most recently second at Goodwood; Jamie Spencer is the ideal partner for a waiting ride, but with the map compressed and no strong pace to close into, his redistribution to midfield captures the reality that this shape may not suit.
runners_data.comment: Huscal won last time out and was second two starts back, which looks encouraging, but he ranks last on our figures in a field of ten and a speed rating of 78 leaves him needing plenty of improvement to trouble the principals here.

runners_data.name: Mister Bluebird
runners_data.note: Heather Main's eight-year-old is the only confirmed front-runner in the race and will dictate the pace from stall to straight; 85 days off is a flag, and headgear (p) has been used before — he has posted two consecutive runner-up finishes on good over 7f here, so course form is strong, but OR=85 means he will be conceding significant weight to most rivals.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Mister Bluebird faces a stiff ask, though runner-up finishes two and three starts back show he can hit the frame, and he has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Archer Royal
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's three-year-old is a confirmed hold-up runner whose recent form includes a third over 7f on good; William Buick takes over which is a clear positive, but the horse's last five runs show finishes of 8-14-7-7-3 — inconsistent and best form came when able to close into a genuine gallop, which this race is unlikely to provide, making his style_fit penalty meaningful.

races.paceDynamic: Mister Bluebird is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no credible challenger for the lead, should dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the gates down Sandown's straight 7f on good ground — the kind of pace that is sustainable rather than sapping. Shameful and Storm Free will sit prominently just behind, likely flanking Mister Bluebird through the first couple of furlongs, but neither has the profile to force a genuine pace battle. This creates a race run at a measured tempo that will leave the lead in clean air and give the closers a single, relatively uniform surge in the final two furlongs rather than a race truly run to suit extremes. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Archer Royal, God Of War, and Huscal are genuine back-of-the-field horses in their natural mode, but with only one pace-setter, space will be tight and at least one or two will find themselves shuffled closer than ideal, reducing their chance of getting a true strong-pace context in which to close. The tactical verdict is clear: a single, uncontested front-runner on good ground at Sandown's straight 7f most favours a prominent racer who can sit just off the controlled gallop, time their run early, and mug the leader — Shameful and Storm Free are the profiles that benefit most from this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Bluebird sets his expected steady tempo and the prominent horses track him unopposed before striking.
scenarios.body: Mister Bluebird controls the race from flag to finish at a fair but not punishing gallop, and Shameful or Storm Free — sitting a length or two off the leader in a position of control — pounce in the final furlong to wear him down or go past; the hold-up horses are simply too far back to reach them in a muted pace scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is even more sedate than expected and Mister Bluebird steals enough of a break that no prominent horse can fully reel him in.
scenarios.body: Mister Bluebird, racing his own race on good ground over a trip and course he clearly favours given back-to-back places here, conserves enough energy through the slow early fractions to repel challengers; the hold-up horses arrive too late and the prominent horses cannot produce a decisive finishing kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Storm Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is surprisingly brisk — perhaps Storm Free or Shameful press Mister Bluebird harder than expected — creating enough of a true gallop to bring the closers into play.
scenarios.body: A stronger tempo would string the field out and leave the prominent horses weakening in the final furlong, opening a clear lane for Desert Shadow or Defence Minister to pick up the pieces late; Desert Shadow's winning form on good ground and Oisin Murphy's tactical awareness make this combination the most dangerous hold-up threat.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If significant market moves, awkward gates, or crowding in the straight disrupts positional plans and forces several horses to race out of their natural style.
scenarios.body: In a scrambled race where positions are contested early, horses with tactical flexibility such as Monarch's Gold or Silver Ghost — who have course-and-distance experience — could benefit from a muddled shape that neutralises the straightforward pace advantage; this scenario is unlikely given one settled front-runner but cannot be entirely dismissed in a competitive 10-runner handicap.

watchPoints.text: Shameful's 436-day layoff is the single biggest unknown in the race — watch the market closely at this is a Clive Cox first-time-out runner with a strong placed record fresh, and if heavily supported it implies stable confidence that could completely reframe the race result.

Mister Bluebird breaks from his gate cleanly or not at all — if he misses the kick and Shameful or Storm Free have to push on to fill the pace vacuum, the tempo will spike and the hold-up horses suddenly become live threats; watch the first furlong carefully.

Desert Shadow with Oisin Murphy is the most obvious market mover in this field given recency of wins and jockey booking — if drifting in the market, suspect the wide draw or fitness concern is flagged by connections; if shortening, treat as dangerous late closer.

Three runners — Archer Royal, God Of War, and Huscal — are genuine hold-up types compressed into a midfield map position; if two or more of these end up on the same rail in the straight fighting for the same closing lane, interference risk rises and could affect the finish order without any of them winning.

Trainer 14-day strike rates flag John & Thady Gosden at 6/23 (active and in form) and Clive Cox at 5/24 — both stables are firing runners in good order at this meeting, which slightly elevates the chances of Archer Royal and Shameful relative to their raw ratings alone.

races.name: Betmgm Real Deal Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Victory Gold
runners_data.note: Won last time at 7f on good ground (Sandown) and is on a retrieval mission from an OR of 87, but must immediately fend off Waasil and Sonny Parvenue from the gate — finishing effort could be blunted by the early battle; Oisin Murphy capable of gauging the pace.
runners_data.comment: Victory Gold showed a sharp return to form when winning two starts back, and a runner-up finish last time out underlines he retains that level; he has experience of today's distance and going, and his rating of 106 marks him as the one to beat from stall 4.

runners_data.name: Waasil
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's yard is firing (10/48 in 14 days) and this horse carries a two-from-two run of form at 7f-8f on good ground; most likely to emerge as the controlling front-runner if rivals get distracted fighting each other, which is his clearest route to victory.

runners_data.name: Sonny Parvenue
runners_data.note: Won on debut at 6f on good but a remote eighth last time at 7f on good ground for Richard Hannon — the step back to his winning distance did not help and the pace rise here looks ominous for a horse that needs to be in front.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win one start back, and Sonny Parvenue has experience over today's trip and going to call on from draw 2 carrying 136 lb; the main concern is a trainer operating at just five per cent in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Noble Prince
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's colt has placed twice at 7f on good but shown no win, and his unknown style means the redistribution to the rear is a structural convenience — Buick will likely push forward from the gate regardless, making his listed position unreliable; lightly raced with upside still possible.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and clearly capable at this level, Noble Prince has run over today's trip and returns after a sharp 14-day turnaround, though he remains winless in recent starts and a mid-field ranking on ratings suggests he faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Dontlookbackinanga
runners_data.note: Two starts, two fourth-place finishes at 7f-8f on good ground for Hannon — no win, limited finishing kick demonstrated, and his style is unclear enough that the rearward redistribution is notional rather than tactical; Sean Levey may elect to chase the pace.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts with a pair of fourth-place finishes, Dontlookbackinanga is ranked bottom of seven on our figures and his trainer is badly out of form at 5% over the past fortnight — hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and distance and going.

runners_data.name: La Fuerza
runners_data.note: Won at 7f on Tapeta (all-weather) last time, earlier placed at 6f on good — Mason Paetel (3lb claimer) holds the mount, which helps with the weight, but this horse will need to immediately engage with three other leaders and its good-ground credentials at 7f are thinner than rivals.
runners_data.comment: La Fuerza arrives here a winner last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, giving him a strong platform; the main risk is the 46-day absence, which leaves fitness to prove under 130 lb from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Clive The Writer
runners_data.note: Won maiden at 7f on Tapeta last time; Lewis Edmunds has the ride for Muir & Grassick who are in fair recent form (2/12), and a prominently-ridden style that sits just off a contested pace could prove ideal if the front-runners exhaust each other — the good-ground profile needs watching.
runners_data.comment: Clive The Writer won last time out but that sole bright spot sits alongside a seventh two starts back, and with a speed rating of 58 ranking him sixth of seven runners, it is hard to build a strong case despite his experience over today's trip and a 24-day break that leaves him fresh.

runners_data.name: Sanbona Warrior
runners_data.note: William Knight's gelding has a solid 7f profile including a win and a second on similar going; Neil Callan partners a horse that tends to race prominently and has the stamina for a strongly-run 7f — positioned well to capitalise if the front-runners tie each other up.
runners_data.comment: Sanbona Warrior won two starts back and was second three starts back, arriving here 21 days later with distance experience and a strong 86 rating to underpin his claims; the fourth last time out is the one blemish to keep in mind.

races.paceDynamic: Victory Gold, Waasil, Sonny Parvenue, and La Fuerza all want to be prominent or lead, meaning this 7f Sandown contest will be ignited from the stalls with four horses immediately competing for the front rank on good ground. That contest for early position will burn through the fuel reserves of every participant, creating a strong, relentless gallop that does not allow any of the pace-setters to coast through the early fractions. The race will be run end-to-end with little respite, and the stamina reserves of the front-runners will be severely tested in the closing stages — the profile this shape most clearly favours is horses who race prominently but have genuine finishing gears or sit just off a contested pace, rather than those who set it outright. Noble Prince and Dontlookbackinanga are listed at the rear but are genuinely unproven stylistically; the field holds far more pace-committed types than can all secure their preferred rail positions, and Victory Gold and Waasil — both winners at 7f on good — are most likely to actually force the early tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the four front-runners fight for supremacy and the gallop is strong enough to string the field out from the halfway point.
scenarios.body: Victory Gold and Waasil immediately lock horns with Sonny Parvenue and La Fuerza, meaning the early fractions are fierce and those who lead are left vulnerable late; the horses who travel just off the pace with stamina reserves — Clive The Writer and Sanbona Warrior — are positioned to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Waasil (the most in-form front-runner, two wins from three) secures a clear lead early and controls the tempo on his own terms.
scenarios.body: Waasil's back-to-back 7f and 8f wins on good ground demonstrate he handles this trip and going well, and if the other front-runners are checked or slot in behind him the pace could be managed rather than combustive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace fully collapses the front four runners in the final furlong and a prominent but slightly held-up runner delivers the decisive challenge.
scenarios.body: Clive The Writer broke his maiden at 7f on Tapeta but has a prominent style that could sit second or third against a contested pace; Sanbona Warrior's form figures of 2-1-4 at 7f suggest he is effective at this trip and capable of a late run when the fractions are truly honest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Noble Prince or Dontlookbackinanga, despite being repositioned to the rear in mapping, prove to have the tactical speed to challenge late once the front-runners have burned each other out.
scenarios.body: Both are lightly raced with unresolved style profiles, and their redistribution to the rear reflects a field imbalance rather than genuine hold-up credentials; this scenario is discounted precisely because neither horse has demonstrated an authentic closing kick at this trip on good ground.

watchPoints.text: Waasil and Victory Gold may immediately clash on the front end — watch whether either gives ground or if both try to force an attritional pace that suits neither.

La Fuerza's first-time appearance at 7f on good turf (previous win was Tapeta) combined with a 3lb claimer under pressure from three rivals at the break could see the colt drop out sharply if the early pace is too fierce.

Noble Prince and Dontlookbackinanga are mapped to the rear by redistribution only — if both push forward from the stalls as expected, the apparent hold-up contingent disappears and Scenario D becomes essentially void.
Clive The Writer's sole win came on an artificial surface; monitor market moves to assess whether connections believe the good turf at Sandown is within his comfort zone before committing.

Sanbona Warrior's headgear notation (hg:p) suggests a change of gear — watch whether this sharpens his early pace to compete more prominently than his mapping suggests, which could further congest an already busy front end.

races.name: Gamble Responsibly At Betmgm Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Betsen
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a mixed recent string including a win and a place at Sandown over 5f on soft earlier this season, but the step up to good going is a noted query given four of the last five runs came on soft or standard; 84 days off the track adds further caution, and Marco Ghiani will need things to fall right late.|
runners_data.comment: Betsen landed a win two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going conditions, with our rating putting him narrowly top of these rivals. The 84-day absence is the one query, but he arrives on an official rating of 86 and looks the one to beat off 139 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Rosario
runners_data.note: Consistent 5f specialist on good going with twelve of fifteen similar-going runs placing, handled this trip well in recent races for Roger Teal, though all five recent runs have produced placings rather than wins and Rossa Ryan will need a clear run from the rear.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Rosario nonetheless rates significantly clear of his official mark on our figures and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, making him a genuine threat from stall eight; the concern is a tendency to find little when it matters.

runners_data.name: Zoulu Chief
runners_data.note: Seven days since last run is a quick turnaround, and the recent form over 6f on good looks a touch below the required level, but Luke Morris has a habit of finding improvement for this trainer and the horse has prior form at a shorter trip in softer conditions; a genuine hold-up type who may need to race more aggressively than preferred.|
runners_data.comment: Zoulu Chief landed a win five starts back and shaped with promise when third four starts back, and he brings distance-and-going experience plus a featherweight 138 lb from stall one; the worry is three consecutive poor efforts since that form.

runners_data.name: Marching Mac
runners_data.note: Winner here at Sandown over 5f on good going last time out and the most immediately relevant form in the race — though 78 days off the track is a concern; Phil McEntee has a quiet 14-day strike rate and this horse's natural style is closer to the rear, meaning it will need to pick its way through on a flat sprint where gaps can close quickly.|

runners_data.name: Quantum Power
runners_data.note: Three wins from five over this exact course and distance on good ground make Quantum Power's profile almost tailor-made; Molly Keegan-Price's 7lb claim softens the weight, though the horse has a visor fitted and is slightly out of natural role as the only confirmed pace-setter in a field with limited front-running competition — position looks assured regardless.|
runners_data.comment: Quantum Power won three of his last six starts, with back-to-back victories two and three starts back, but a ninth last time out tempers enthusiasm; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 136 lb from stall four, and returns after 30 days off.

runners_data.name: Hypnotised
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old who showed smart early speed when winning at 5f on Tapeta and has two runner-up finishes at this trip on good, so the going holds no fears; Harry Charlton's stable is in decent form (5 from 19 in 14 days) and Lewis Edmunds is a competent handler, though the horse's hold-up tendency means it will need a smooth passage that cannot be guaranteed.|
runners_data.comment: Hypnotised has been knocking on the door in his last two starts and, having run over today's trip and going, arrives in fine nick just a fortnight since his last outing; the main risk is whether he can convert that consistent placing form into a win off 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Lipsink
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's nine-year-old is a proven course-and-distance winner on good ground and ran just eight days ago, suggesting Appleby has him primed; Alistair Rawlinson can ride prominently and the horse's record of 1W4P from eight good-ground runs gives him strong place credentials over forcing tactics from close to the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Lipsink has been unplaced last time out and, ranked eighth of ten on our figures, is hard to fancy at the weights, though he does bring distance and going experience and back-to-back wins earlier in this recent sequence show he can find the winner's enclosure.

runners_data.name: Nuevo Slovo
runners_data.note: Apprentice Paddy Bradley partners a horse whose last five runs are all placings or defeats on good ground at 5-6f, with a 6f win on good as the career highlight; natural hold-up style pushed to the midfield map position, which is accurate because the rear is overcrowded, and Simon Pearce's low-volume stable has limited ammunition for a race this competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Nuevo Slovo at least shaped more encouragingly last time with a fourth, and he has experience of today's distance and going; a mark of 78 and 129 lb from stall seven make this far from straightforward, though.

runners_data.name: Roach Power
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran with two career wins on good going but recent form reading 0-9-7-4-10 paints a picture of a horse who has fallen below the level needed here; redistributed from the rear because of field congestion at the back, Michael Wigham's charge will need something to go very wrong for others to threaten from his natural position.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Roach Power faces a stiff task here; the consolations are a return to familiar distance and going conditions, and he comes here fit enough on a 14-day turnaround carrying 129 lb from stall three.

runners_data.name: Havana Smile
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore's three-year-old won over 5f on good ground and has place form at the course, making the form relevant, but apprentice Toby Moore (7lb claim) is on a horse that settles naturally at the back and 37 days between runs adds a fitness question; the hold-up style is genuine and the horse has been squeezed into a midfield map slot by virtue of the crowded rear division.|
runners_data.comment: Havana Smile has finished fifth and sixth in his last two starts and ranks bottom of the field on our figures, making him hard to fancy despite a win three starts back and experience over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Quantum Power is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to push them from the off, Molly Keegan-Price (claiming 7lb) can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this flat Sandown 5f. The pace will be honest but not fierce, meaning the early fractions are unlikely to be extreme enough to gift a dramatic late surge to horses coming from off the bridle. Lipsink and Zoulu Chief have shown enough prominent/forcing tendencies to sit close to the pace, and they represent the most likely challengers to Quantum Power's positional advantage through the middle portion of the race. This shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or making their move from a stalking position — a clean, mid-tempo lead with no pressure loading creates a front-runners' and prominent racers' race at this flat track. Five horses — Marching Mac, Hypnotised, Nuevo Slovo, Roach Power and Havana Smile — are true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because the field is rear-heavy; of those, Marching Mac and Hypnotised are most likely to actually secure a closer tracking position given their recent form and connections' intent.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Quantum Power Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Quantum Power secures the lead without early pressure and sets a controlled pace that suits a prominent run.
scenarios.body: Quantum Power travels smoothly on the front end and, with no rival able or willing to take them on, the tempo remains within the horse's comfort zone before quickening out of the dip; the three-year-old's three wins from five over this exact course-and-distance combination and good-going record make this profile deeply credible.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalkers Peg Back Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Lipsink or Zoulu Chief travel prominently behind Quantum Power and outstay them in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A just-sustainable early tempo leaves Quantum Power exposed late as Lipsink, a proven course-and-distance winner who is fresh off an eight-day turnaround, picks up from a handy position; Zoulu Chief, quick into stride and with good-ground credentials, could also arrive on the scene as a second finisher without ever hitting the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If pace collapses and the moderate tempo produces a late sprint that rewards the one true closer who gets clear daylight.
scenarios.body: This is a difficult shape to execute given the field's rear-heavy profile means multiple horses will be hunting gaps simultaneously; Marching Mac, winner here over 5f on good going and the most experienced hold-up performer in the field, or Hypnotised, lightly raced and with a runner-up finish on this course, would be the most plausible beneficiaries if a gap materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse and Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for position creates a bunched midfield and the race degenerates into a rough sprint finish.
scenarios.body: With five redistributed hold-up types all searching for cover and a controlling front-runner, any stumble or interference in the early stages could scramble the expected shape and open the door to a complete outsider; Havana Smile, a course-and-distance winner at 5f on good ground for the Moores despite today's apprentice rider, or Rosario, consistent at the trip in this going band, could capitalise on fortune.

watchPoints.text: Quantum Power's early position is critical — if anything rushes them or they miss the break, the entire pace shape unravels and hold-up horses like Marching Mac suddenly look live dangers.

Lipsink has run just eight days ago and Alistair Rawlinson may push to travel prominently; watch whether he gets the rail or a clear pitch behind Quantum Power in the early strides, as that will define the race's tempo.

With five hold-up types competing for the same late ground, Marching Mac and Hypnotised are most likely to get daylight — but congestion in the straight could cost all of them a clear run simultaneously.

Molly Keegan-Price's 7lb claim means Quantum Power carries 136lbs, reduced to 129lb effective — monitor whether the apprentice over-commits early or settles confidently, as the front-runner's ability to control pace is the single biggest factor in the race shape.

Zoulu Chief's quick seven-day turnaround for Heather Main and Luke Morris is worth noting — horses returned rapidly are sometimes cherry-picked for a specific ground or pace scenario, and this horse's hold-up profile may see Morris try an atypically forward ride if the early gallop is sufficiently modest.
